teaching_structure.teaching_activities:
Introduce the compound angle identities for sine and cosine:
    sin(A+B)=sinAcosB+cosAsinB
    sin(A-B)=sinAcosB-cosAsinB
    cos(A+B)=cosAcosB-sinAsinB
    cos(A-B)=cosAcosB+sinAsinB

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Ask students to derive the identity for sin(A-B) using the identity for sin(A+B) and the fact that sin(-B)=-sinB and cos(-B)=cosB.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Attempt the derivation of sin(A-B). Individually or in pairs, create a trigonometry problem that is best solved using a sine or cosine compound angle identity.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities:
Review the compound angle identities for sine and cosine. Introduce the compound angle identity for tangent:
    tan(A+B)=1-tanAtanBtanA+tanB​
    tan(A-B)=1+tanAtanBtanA-tanB​

teaching_structure.teaching_activities:

    cos(2A)=cos2A-sin2A=2cos2A-1=1-2sin2A
    tan(2A)=1-tan2A​
